title: How Wind Turbines Make Electricity
meta_description: Learn how turbine blades capture wind, turn a generator, connect to the electricity grid, and why wind speed and turbine design affect power output.
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: Wind turbine blades work mainly through aerodynamic lift, much as an aircraft wing does, rather than simply being pushed like a flat sail.
The rotor turns a shaft connected to a generator directly or through a gearbox; generator designs convert mechanical rotation into electrical energy.
Power available in wind rises roughly with the cube of wind speed before turbine and control limits are considered, so small speed changes can make large output differences.
Electricity typically passes through power electronics and transformers before reaching the grid, and the turbine shuts down or limits output in conditions outside its safe operating range.
